questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The policy aims to neither penalise first-time offenders (1)/ nor those who may have violated norms (2)/ due to systemic ambiguity (3)/ rather than deliberate intent. (4)
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The policy aims to neither penalise first-time offenders (1)/ nor those who may have violated norms (2)/ due to systemic ambiguity (3)/ rather than deliberate intent. (4)
questions.solution: The correct answer is: -1. Option 1 is correct because "neither" is misplaced, creating a parallelism error. To maintain balance with the second part of the sentence ("nor those who..."), "neither" should be placed after the verb "penalise." The sentence should correctly read: "The policy aims to penalise neither first-time offenders nor those who may have violated norms..."

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: It was not merely the fragmentation of administrative jurisdictions across sectors (1)/ that disrupted cohesive governance, but the inertia embedded in overlapping regulatory mandates (2)/ which, though designed to safeguard institutional autonomy, (3)/ ends up paralyzing inter-departmental responsiveness altogether. (4)
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

It was not merely the fragmentation of administrative jurisdictions across sectors (1)/ that disrupted cohesive governance, but the inertia embedded in overlapping regulatory mandates (2)/ which, though designed to safeguard institutional autonomy, (3)/ ends up paralyzing inter-departmental responsiveness altogether. (4)
questions.solution: The correct answer is: -4. Option 4 is correct because it contains a subject-verb agreement and tense error. The verb "ends" is singular, but its subject is "overlapping regulatory mandates" (plural) in part 2. The phrase "ends up" is inconsistent in tense with the rest of the sentence, which is in the past tense. "It was not merely the fragmentation... but the inertia embedded in overlapping regulatory mandates which, though designed to safeguard institutional autonomy, ended up paralyzing inter-departmental responsiveness altogether."

questions.question: Change the following from active to passive: The committee had been debating complex amendments when the bell rang.
questions.questionHtml:
Change the following from active to passive:

The committee had been debating complex amendments when the bell rang.

options.text: Complex amendments had had been been debated by the committee when the bell rang.
options.html: Complex amendments had had been been debated by the committee when the bell rang.

options.text: Complex amendments had been being debated by the committee when the bell rang.
options.html: Complex amendments had been being debated by the committee when the bell rang.

options.text: Complex amendments had be being debated by the committee when the bell rang.
options.html: Complex amendments had be being debated by the committee when the bell rang.

options.text: Complex amendments had debated by the committee when the bell rang.
options.html: Complex amendments had debated by the committee when the bell rang.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 - Complex amendments had been being debated by the committee when the bell rang.

This conversion is from Active to Passive.

 Explanation of the change in form:
The active voice sentence is in Past Perfect Continuous tense (Subject + had been + V-ing + Object). When converted to passive voice, the tense remains Past Perfect Continuous, but the structure changes to:  
Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + had been being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

Here:
- Active Voice: The committee (Subject) had been debating (Past Perfect Continuous) complex amendments (Object).  
- Passive Voice: Complex amendments (Object from active voice, now Subject in passive voice) had been being debated (Past Perfect Continuous Passive) by the committee (Subject from active voice, now Object in passive voice).

questions.question: Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure: A letter is written to the editor by the citizen every week.
questions.questionHtml:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

A letter is written to the editor by the citizen every week.

options.text: The editor writes a letter to the citizen every week.
options.html: The editor writes a letter to the citizen every week.

options.text: The citizen writes a letter to the editor every week.
options.html: The citizen writes a letter to the editor every week.

options.text: The editor wrote a letter every week.
options.html: The editor wrote a letter every week.

options.text: The citizen has been writing letters to the editor weekly.
options.html: The citizen has been writing letters to the editor weekly.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: The citizen writes a letter to the editor every week.  
Conversion: Passive to Active.  

Explanation: The sentence in the question is in Passive voice, Present Indefinite tense (Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject). The conversion to Active voice rearranges the sentence to focus on the subject performing the action (Subject + V1/V5 + Object). In this case, "the citizen" becomes the subject performing the action "writes," and "the editor" becomes the object receiving the action.

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph: 1. This makes them ideal for tasks like image recognition, natural language processing, and medical diagnostics. 2. Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that focuses on the creation of algorithms that can learn from data without explicit programming. 3. The algorithm improves its performance by analyzing vast amounts of input data and identifying underlying patterns. 4. Instead of being given a set of rules, a machine learning model is trained on examples.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph:

1. This makes them ideal for tasks like image recognition, natural language processing, and medical diagnostics.

2. Machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence that focuses on the creation of algorithms that can learn from data without explicit programming.

3. The algorithm improves its performance by analyzing vast amounts of input data and identifying underlying patterns.

4. Instead of being given a set of rules, a machine learning model is trained on examples.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: 2, 4, 3, 1.

Explanation of Chronology:
1. Sentence 2: Introduces the concept of machine learning as a subset of artificial intelligence, setting the foundation for the discussion.
2. Sentence 4: Explains the training process of machine learning models, which naturally follows after introducing the concept.
3. Sentence 3: Describes how the algorithm improves its performance through analyzing data, building on the training process mentioned in Sentence 4.
4. Sentence 1: Highlights the practical applications of machine learning, which logically concludes the paragraph after explaining the process.

Why the correct answer is in the right position:
Each sentence builds upon the previous one—starting with the concept (Sentence 2), then the process (Sentences 4 and 3), and finally the applications (Sentence 1). This ensures a coherent progression of ideas.

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph: 1. The primary purpose of this process is to ensure that the food we eat is safe and does not contain harmful bacteria or other contaminants. 2. Food processing is a series of methods used to transform raw ingredients into consumable products. 3. These methods can range from simple actions like cutting and grinding to more complex procedures such as pasteurization and fermentation. 4. Furthermore, it also helps to preserve food, extend its shelf life, and enhance its nutritional value.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph:

1. The primary purpose of this process is to ensure that the food we eat is safe and does not contain harmful bacteria or other contaminants.

2. Food processing is a series of methods used to transform raw ingredients into consumable products.

3. These methods can range from simple actions like cutting and grinding to more complex procedures such as pasteurization and fermentation.

4. Furthermore, it also helps to preserve food, extend its shelf life, and enhance its nutritional value.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: 2, 3, 1, 4.  

The chronology follows this order because:  
- Sentence 2 introduces the concept of food processing as a transformation process of raw ingredients into consumable products.  
- Sentence 3 elaborates on the methods involved, moving from simple to complex procedures.  
- Sentence 1 explains the primary purpose of the process, focusing on safety and contamination prevention.  
- Sentence 4 adds further benefits like preservation, shelf life extension, and enhanced nutrition.  

The correct positions align as Sentence 2 sets the foundation, Sentence 3 provides details, Sentence 1 explains the main purpose, and Sentence 4 concludes with additional advantages, creating a logical progression of ideas.
